answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by implementing a unique work grading mechanism. Each identity must submit original work evaluated by established peers who stake tokens against it. As more identities emerge, the cost increases due to the need for additional endorsements to verify submissions. This trend continues, quickly leading to costs exceeding 1,000 tokens. It's akin to navigating a narrow inlet into a vast ocean; the more vessels (fakes) that try to enter, the more congestion and difficulty they face at the ridge, ultimately leading to their failure.
